description: Backend-aware per-phase model resolution plus config-tolerant drift/review guards so a codex-backed phase can be committed without reddening bun test (CAM-54 slice-5).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.TOML.parse is the canonical parser (confirmed via the Bun APIs index -> Parsing & Formatting -> Bun.TOML.parse at /runtime/toml). A TOML sub-table header like [models.codex] parses to a nested plain object under the parent key (standard TOML semantics), so the schema-less loadConfig layer returns models.codex as an object; the flat models[phase] lookup must type-guard and skip that object rather than mis-return it as a model string.

userStories.title: Make readPhaseModel backend-aware
userStories.description: As the cam loop, I need per-phase model resolution to consult the phase's resolved backend so a codex phase resolves a codex-valid slug from a nested [models.<backend>] sub-table, while claude phases keep resolving the flat [models].<phase> / DEFAULTS value unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: readPhaseModel accepts the phase's already-resolved backend and, when that backend is non-claude and a nested [models.<backend>].<phase> key is present, returns it; otherwise it falls back to the flat [models].<phase> value then DEFAULTS[phase]. A unit test proves a codex-backed phase resolves the codex slug from a [models.codex] fixture and that claude-phase resolution (and every existing readPhaseModel call passing only phase/configPath) is byte-for-byte unchanged. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]

The flat models[phase] lookup skips a nested object value (a [models.codex] sub-table parses to typeof 'object') and falls through to DEFAULTS instead of returning the object as a model string; the nested backend-aware lookup is type-guarded against the schema-less TOML layer (no assumption of shape). A unit test covers a config where [models.codex] is present but the requested phase is claude-backed. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]
DEFAULTS is not modified. [oracle: file-assert git diff scripts/cam/project.toml is empty and DEFAULTS block unchanged: git diff --exit-code scripts/cam/project.toml]
Committed scripts/cam/project.toml is byte-unchanged (no [models.codex] table added). [oracle: file-assert git diff --exit-code scripts/cam/project.toml]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/config/models.ts (readPhaseModel, lines 110-125), test/config/models.test.ts. Signature guidance: current readPhaseModel(phase, configPath?) has ~17 callers passing configPath (mostly tests); add the resolved backend as a NEW optional 3rd param (readPhaseModel(phase, configPath?, backend?)) so no existing (phase, configPath) caller breaks. When backend is omitted or 'claude', behavior must be identical to today. Nested lookup: config['models'][backend]?.[phase], type-guarded (typeof object on models, typeof string on the value), BEFORE the flat models[phase] lookup; the flat lookup must reject a typeof-object value (the sub-table) and fall through to DEFAULTS. TOML layer is schema-less (src/config/toml.ts:135-157, Bun.TOML.parse, no validation): do not assume shape. Pattern context: [models]/[backend] config surface + read-at-spawn invariant (patterns.md, CAM-53 US-008). Do NOT change DEFAULTS or MODEL_OPTIONS.

userStories.title: Thread resolved backend into readPhaseModel at every dispatch site
userStories.description: As the cam loop, I need every spawn site that resolves both model and backend to pass the resolved backend into readPhaseModel, so a codex phase never receives a claude-alias model at spawn.
acceptanceCriteria: Each dispatch site that resolves a phase's model and backend passes the resolved backend into readPhaseModel: reviewer (src/supervisor/review.ts:351-352), implementer (src/supervisor/loop.ts:1051-1052), planner and auditor (src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:626-627 and 681-682), orchestrator (src/commands/run.ts:453), and the config display column (src/commands/config.ts:297). userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/review.ts, src/supervisor/loop.ts, src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts, src/commands/run.ts, src/commands/config.ts. Mechanical single-concern spread: each site already resolves the backend right beside the model (readPhaseBackend beside readPhaseModel, e.g. review.ts reviewBackend, loop.ts implBackend) for selectAdapter; this story only threads that same backend var into the readPhaseModel call. Passes only the backend the site already resolved: no new backend read. Confirm the committed config keeps all phases claude, so this is behavior-preserving for the committed toml (the tolerance only manifests under a codex fixture, proved in US-004). Pattern context: spawn-resolution emitter (patterns.md, CAM-53 US-007) reports the resolved model+backend; keep the two reads consistent (the reviewer double-read finding).

userStories.title: Make the drift guard backend-conditional and config-tolerant
userStories.description: As the test suite, I need the readPhaseModel drift guard to validate a codex-backed phase as a non-claude-alias model (rather than against the claude MODEL_OPTIONS list) so a future codex flip does not falsely redden the suite, while claude phases keep their MODEL_OPTIONS/DEFAULTS check.
acceptanceCriteria: isClaudeAliasModel is exported from src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts (previously module-private). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'export function isClaudeAliasModel' src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts]

The drift guard in test/config/models.test.ts is backend-conditional: for a phase whose resolved backend (readPhaseBackend) is non-claude, the resolved model is accepted iff isClaudeAliasModel(model) is false; for a claude-backed phase the model is still required to be in MODEL_OPTIONS or equal DEFAULTS[phase]. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]
The adjacent 'DEFAULTS vs MODEL_OPTIONS consistency' guard (models.test.ts:646-656) is unchanged and still passes. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]
src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx MODEL_OPTIONS contains no codex model slugs (no gpt- ids). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qi 'gpt-' src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx]

userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts (export isClaudeAliasModel, lines 79-82: the CLAUDE_ALIAS_MODEL_RE guard), test/config/models.test.ts (drift guard, lines 667-684). Do NOT add a positive codex-slug allowlist: OpenAI slugs are account-specific and drift (gpt-5.5/gpt-5.6-sol valid, all *-codex rejected on this login), so assert NOT isClaudeAliasModel for codex phases (FORK B resolved in the issue gotchas). The drift guard reads readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath); to be tolerant it must branch on readPhaseBackend(phase, repoConfigPath). Committed config stays all-claude so every phase still takes the claude branch today. Do not change DEFAULTS.

userStories.title: Generalize the review-fixture helper and prove codex reviewer resolution
